svg.text: talk.01 · ROUND 3 · SILHOUETTE LINEUP
six deliberately different shapes · judge the shape first, details second
TENTATIVE · NOT A FINAL DESIGN
original concepts · same scale in every card (10 mm = 30 px)
LOGO TEST: in solid black, can you tell them apart, and does one make you want to pick it up?
FLIP
TILT
CUT
LAYERS
WEDGE (side)
PEBBLE
1 · FLIP
a clamshell that changes shape: closed, desk L, straight
hero: the seam and the orange hinge barrels; it transforms
closed = pocket-safe + muted · L = desk mic · straight = handheld
stand: the hinge itself · cover: small hatch under the base
+ pager-clamshell nostalgia, fully protected when closed
+ the pose is the mode (hinge angle sensor)
- needs a friction/detent hinge that FDM can hold
- thin blocks (about 14 mm) pack electronics tightly
2 · TILT
a grip and a head: the head tilts to aim at your mouth
hero: the two-block shape with an orange joint
head tilts +-30° in detents · EQ-bar grille is the identity
stand: a short foot (small U) · cover: round hatch in the grip
+ solves 'aim at the mouth' with a toy-like mechanism
+ strong silhouette and a fun joint to fidget with
- joint strength and the cable moving with the head
- more parts than any slab
3 · CUT
one 30° angle used on everything, plus a big slanted lever
hero: the chamfered corner with the dial, and the wedge lever
every cut, slot and the hatch corner share one angle
cover = stand: the small hatch swings out as the kickstand
+ logo-like silhouette; one motif = strong identity
+ opening the stand opens the bay: one action
- the bay is exposed whenever the stand is out
- wedge lever is close to the reference's idea
4 · LAYERS
three stacked plates, colour-blocked, screws as ornament
hero: the colour-blocked stack and the exposed screws
top plate = grille, middle = controls, bottom = base + battery
stand: small U on the middle plate · cover: the bottom plate
+ print each plate in a different colour; swap to customise
+ the cover idea becomes the whole identity
- alignment of three parts; seams must look deliberate
- the stack look can feel generic without the details
5 · WEDGE
a doorstop: the body is the stand, no mechanism at all
hero: the doorstop profile and three big round holes
front face leans back about 21°; battery lives in the heavy base
stand: none needed · cover: the base plate underneath
+ nothing to break; very stable; low centre of mass
+ a desk object with a clear face
- bulky in a bag; not a folding stand (changes the brief)
- handheld shape is a wedge in the palm: needs a mock
6 · PEBBLE
a round puck: the bezel ring turns for the mode
hero: the circle, the turning bezel and the arc lever
ring marks DICT / TALK / OPEN / LOCK; a flat foot stops rolling
stand: a small U ring on the back · cover: round hatch
+ the most distinct silhouette; fits a pocket and a palm
+ bezel is a great fidget; arc lever follows the thumb
- furthest from the pager/radio feel; round parts are harder
- rolling and thumb reach need physical mocks
